The Hidden Cost of Applying to the Wrong Company Stage Jobgether Read this article on LinkedIn to join the conversation Read on LinkedIn A senior professional with a strong background can apply to ten well-matched roles and land two interviews, or apply to ten structurally mismatched roles and land zero, with an identical resume in both cases. The difference is not the resume. It is company stage, and it is one of the least discussed filters in a senior job search. Executive Failure Is Well Documented. Executive Mistargeting Is Not Kevin Kelly, CEO of Heidrick & Struggles, has said the firm's own placement data shows forty percent of executives hired at the senior level are pushed out, fail, or quit within eighteen months, with stage mismatch a recurring driver. That statistic describes what happens after an offer. Almost no one talks about how many strong candidates never reach an offer at all, because their search targeted a stage that was never going to select for their specific background in the first place. Four Stages, Four Different Hiring Briefs Early-stage companies need someone who builds structure from nothing. Growth-stage companies need someone who has scaled a function once and can install process without slowing things down. Enterprise and public companies need depth within a narrow scope and comfort with consensus across a complex org chart. PE-backed companies need comfort with a specific, board-reportable value-creation timeline, typically a three to five year hold. The same strong background can be read as an asset at one of these and a liability at another, and the difference has nothing to do with how the resume is written. ...
